```{=html}
<div class="fv-takeaway">Make additions inspectable; more detail can also change the request.</div>
<div class="fv-source"><a href="https://huggingface.co/black-forest-labs/flux-3-image-klein">FLUX 3 prompt upsampling</a> · <a href="https://huggingface.co/spaces/black-forest-labs/flux-3-image-klein/blob/77e15faba0d6ef8d07ff53b5c19e256ef2ff757f/app.py">Official demo prompts</a> · <a href="https://openai.com/index/video-generation-models-as-world-simulators/">Sora language understanding</a></div>
```

::: {.notes}
The short request and ‘No text’ constraint are invented teaching inputs.

**First click: the intermediate caption.** Reveal the proposed camera, lighting, material and background details while preserving the user's cup, table and no-text requirements.

**Second click: separate original constraints from system-proposed additions.** The labels identify which details came from the user and which were added. Ask which additions could change the intended scene.

**Third click: training-caption connection and teaching mockup.** The richer generator input resembles a detailed training caption. The mockup is an original vector illustration, not a measured model result; the no-text constraint remains unchanged.

FLUX 3's model card describes prompt upsampling as an external stage converting a request and optional image references into a full scene caption. Its official demo exposes text-only and image-conditioned system prompts. Detailed captions connect to the earlier recaptioning example on D 33: training descriptions and generator inputs can share a richer format. The Sora report likewise describes recaptioning and expanding short user prompts.

The expansion is an additional system call, not a mandatory internal ability of all image models. A richer caption does not guarantee a better result. Students should identify which details were supplied by the user, which were inferred, and which fixed requirements must remain unchanged.

Sources (checked 21 October 2026): [FLUX 3 prompt upsampling](https://huggingface.co/black-forest-labs/flux-3-image-klein); [Official demo prompts](https://huggingface.co/spaces/black-forest-labs/flux-3-image-klein/blob/77e15faba0d6ef8d07ff53b5c19e256ef2ff757f/app.py); [Sora language understanding](https://openai.com/index/video-generation-models-as-world-simulators/).
:::

## Programmatic multimodal data {#frontier-f17 .fv-slide background-color="#ffffff"}

```{=html}
<div class="fv-meta"><span class="fv-id">D 36 / 42</span><span class="fv-cluster">Architecture</span><span class="fv-cluster active">Data</span><span class="fv-cluster">Training</span><span class="fv-cluster">Inference</span><span class="fv-cluster">Tools</span></div>
<div class="fv-body f17-body">
  <div class="f17-pair"><div class="f17-code"><b>SVG source</b><code>&lt;<mark class="fragment fv-highlight" data-fragment-index="1">circle</mark> cx="80" cy="50" r="32" /&gt;</code></div><div class="f17-render">→ <span>Renderer</span> →</div><div class="f17-result"><b>Image</b><svg viewBox="0 0 250 100" width="250" height="100" role="img" aria-label="A circle rendered from SVG"><rect x="8" y="8" width="234" height="84" fill="#fff" stroke="#c5c5c5"/><circle class="f17-shape fragment fv-highlight" data-fragment-index="1" cx="80" cy="50" r="32" fill="#e5e5e5" stroke="#141414"/></svg></div></div>
  <div class="f17-pair"><div class="f17-code"><b>Webpage structure</b><code>&lt;header /&gt; &lt;<mark class="fragment fv-highlight" data-fragment-index="2">button</mark>&gt;Go&lt;/button&gt;</code></div><div class="f17-render">→ <span>Renderer</span> →</div><div class="f17-result"><b>Screenshot</b><svg viewBox="0 0 250 100" width="250" height="100" role="img" aria-label="Page markup rendered as a screenshot with a button"><rect x="8" y="8" width="234" height="84" fill="#fff" stroke="#c5c5c5"/><rect x="8" y="8" width="234" height="17" fill="#141414"/><path d="M25 40H150M25 50H125" stroke="#bcbcbc" stroke-width="3"/><rect class="f17-shape fragment fv-highlight" data-fragment-index="2" x="150" y="52" width="74" height="30" fill="#e5e5e5" stroke="#141414"/><text x="187" y="76" text-anchor="middle" font-size="24" fill="#141414">Go</text></svg></div></div>
  <div class="f17-pair"><div class="f17-code"><b>Scene description</b><code>plane + <mark class="fragment fv-highlight" data-fragment-index="3">sphere</mark> + camera + light</code></div><div class="f17-render">→ <span>Renderer</span> →</div><div class="f17-result"><b>Rendered scene</b><svg viewBox="0 0 250 100" width="250" height="100" role="img" aria-label="A scene description linked to an image of a sphere on a plane"><defs><radialGradient id="f17-sphere-light" cx="32%" cy="25%"><stop offset="0" stop-color="#fff"/><stop offset="1" stop-color="#141414"/></radialGradient></defs><path d="M15 84L87 35L238 71L190 94Z" fill="#eee" stroke="#c5c5c5"/><ellipse cx="134" cy="78" rx="44" ry="9" fill="#c5c5c5"/><circle cx="121" cy="49" r="31" fill="url(#f17-sphere-light)"/><circle class="f17-sphere-ring fragment" data-fragment-index="3" cx="121" cy="49" r="35" fill="none" stroke="#bef264" stroke-width="5"/></svg></div></div>
  <div class="f17-other">Complements the corpus: <span>Caption</span><span>OCR</span><span>Interleaved documents</span><span>Video</span></div>
</div>
<div class="fv-takeaway">Rendering creates a controlled link between structure and visual output.</div>
<div class="fv-source"><a href="https://arxiv.org/html/2607.24653v1#S3.SS1">Kimi K3, §3.1, 2026</a> · <a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2206.06994">ProcTHOR, 2022</a> · Teaching illustrations</div>
```

::: {.notes}
An image can have a structured source: a vector description, page markup, or scene parameters. If we control that source, we can produce linked data through the process that creates the image.

Look at the three independent rows. In the first, SVG describes a circle through its center and radius. A renderer turns that description into an image. In the second, the page structure defines the elements that appear in the screenshot. In the third, scene objects, a camera, and lighting determine the visual output.

*Three clicks link circle to the circle, button to the button, and sphere to the sphere, in sequence.*

Programmatic annotation means computing the required label from known structure or geometry. For example, object coordinates are available before any visual recognition takes place. This lets us produce consistent pairs of images and descriptions or coordinate labels.

The image also depends on rendering conditions: fonts, scale, camera, and lighting. We need to account for the actual output the model will see. Controlled examples complement the captions, OCR, documents, and video listed below. They do not automatically cover the full diversity of real images. Next, we change one value in the source and see how the image and the answer change together.

**Sources:** [Kimi K3, §3.1, 2026](https://arxiv.org/html/2607.24653v1#S3.SS1), [ProcTHOR, 2022](https://arxiv.org/abs/2206.06994).
:::

```{=html}
<div class="fv-body mv-body mv28-body mv-steady fragment" data-fragment-index="2">
  <div class="mv28-code"><h3>DATA + CODE</h3><div class="mv28-values"><p>A = <span class="mv-switch"><span class="fragment fade-out" data-fragment-index="2">12</span><span class="fragment" data-fragment-index="2">27</span></span></p><p>B = 21</p><p>C = 9</p></div><pre>labels = ["A", "B", "C"]
values = [A, B, C]
render_bar_chart(values)
build_qa(values)</pre><p class="mv-small">Preparation source</p></div>
  <div class="mv28-branches"><div><i>→</i><b>RENDER</b><i>→</i></div><div><i>→</i><b>BUILD Q&amp;A</b><i>→</i></div></div>
  <div class="mv28-example mv-frame-steady fragment" data-fragment-index="1"><h3 class="fragment" data-fragment-index="1">TRAINING EXAMPLE</h3><svg class="mv28-chart" viewBox="0 0 560 290" role="img" aria-label="Teaching bar chart. Initially A equals 12, B equals 21 and C equals 9. On the second click A changes to 27."><g stroke="#d7d7d7" stroke-width="1"><path d="M66 56H516M66 116H516M66 176H516"/></g><path d="M66 40V236H516" fill="none" stroke="#626262" stroke-width="2"/><g fill="#626262" font-size="19" text-anchor="end"><text x="53" y="243">0</text><text x="53" y="183">10</text><text x="53" y="123">20</text><text x="53" y="63">30</text></g><rect class="mv28-bar-a" x="100" y="164" width="90" height="72"/><rect class="mv28-bar-b" x="240" y="110" width="90" height="126"/><rect x="380" y="182" width="90" height="54" fill="#8b8b8b"/><g fill="#141414" font-size="25" text-anchor="middle"><text class="fragment fade-out" data-fragment-index="2" x="145" y="151">12</text><text class="fragment" data-fragment-index="2" x="145" y="61">27</text><text x="285" y="97">21</text><text x="425" y="169">9</text><text x="145" y="271">A</text><text x="285" y="271">B</text><text x="425" y="271">C</text></g></svg><p class="mv28-question">Which category has the highest value?</p><div class="mv28-answer fragment" data-fragment-index="1">Answer: <span class="mv-switch"><span class="fragment fade-out" data-fragment-index="2">B</span><span class="fragment" data-fragment-index="2">A</span></span></div></div>
  <p class="mv28-check">Check that the answer is visible in the rendered image. <b>Measured · Molmo, 11 benchmarks: + PixMo-Docs 72.5 → 74.0</b></p>
</div>
<div class="fv-takeaway fragment" data-fragment-index="2">One source. An image and a checkable answer.</div>
<div class="fv-source"><a href="https://arxiv.org/html/2409.17146v2#S3">Molmo and PixMo, PixMo-Docs; Appendix F</a> · <a href="https://arxiv.org/html/2502.13923">Qwen2.5-VL, §2.2.1, OCR Data</a> · Original teaching example</div>
```

::: {.notes}
One preparation source branches into rendering and question construction. The teaching values are A=12, B=21, C=9. The chart and question are visible before the answer is revealed.

**First click.** The chart, question and answer B form one TRAINING EXAMPLE. The source code stays outside its border. It is available during data preparation, not supplied as a shortcut to the model answering this visual question.

**Second click.** A changes to 27; its bar and visible numerical label update, and the answer changes to A. B and C remain unchanged. The result is computed from the same values as the rendering. This animation is an exact illustrative calculation, not a sample from a released corpus. Source access does not guarantee that all generated questions are visually answerable: the required information must survive the rendering.

PixMo-Docs uses programs to render data and gives code to an LLM for question generation. Qwen2.5-VL separately reports programmatically synthesized charts. The latter is supporting evidence for chart generation, not an attribution of PixMo's exact question-generation method.

The effect is measured. Adding these code-rendered images with questions to academic fine-tuning data raises Molmo's average over 11 benchmarks from 72.5 to 74.0; removing them from the full mixture lowers it from 76.9 to 75.8. Next, one report shows that different visual skills need different pipelines.

Sources: [PixMo-Docs, §3 and Appendix F](https://arxiv.org/html/2409.17146v2); [Qwen2.5-VL, §2.2.1](https://arxiv.org/html/2502.13923).

MIDI events can generate synthesized audio and exactly aligned pitch, onset and duration labels from one program source. [YuE2 Appendix B](https://arxiv.org/html/2609.33757v1) uses human annotations and MIDI renders to train SheetSage2-Prober, then applies it to real recordings to create pseudo-labels for SheetSage2-AR. Exact generated labels describe the rendered sound; predicted labels for real performances can be wrong, and MIDI alone guarantees neither performance details nor data-use rights.
:::

## Charts, tables, pages: one pipeline per visual skill {#data-visual-pipelines .fv-slide background-color="#ffffff"}

```{=html}
<div class="fv-meta"><span class="fv-id">D 38 / 42</span><span class="fv-cluster">Architecture</span><span class="fv-cluster active">Data</span><span class="fv-cluster">Training</span><span class="fv-cluster">Inference</span><span class="fv-cluster">Tools</span></div>
<div class="fv-body dc-body">
  <div class="dc-kicker"><b>Qwen2.5-VL · three OCR data pipelines</b><span>Reported recipe · §2.2.1</span></div>
  <div class="dc-two dc-three">
    <div class="dc-recipe"><h3>Charts: generate</h3><div class="dc-metric"><b class="dc-number">1M</b><span>synthetic</span></div><p><code>matplotlib · seaborn · plotly</code></p><p>Control chart type and data values.</p></div>
    <div class="dc-recipe"><h3>Tables: recognize, filter</h3><div class="dc-metric"><b class="dc-number">6M</b><span>real, before filtering</span></div><p>A model recovers table structure.</p><p class="dc-caption">Drop low confidence, overlaps, low cell density.</p></div>
    <div class="dc-recipe"><h3>Pages: define the target</h3><div class="dc-metric"><b class="dc-number">HTML</b></div><p>Text and formulas · blocks and tables · block coordinates · illustration descriptions.</p></div>
  </div>
</div>
<div class="fv-takeaway">The target annotation defines the skill; each skill gets its own pipeline.</div>
<div class="fv-source"><a href="https://arxiv.org/html/2502.13923#S2.SS2.SSS1">Qwen2.5-VL Technical Report, §2.2.1 — OCR Data and Document Omni-Parsing Data, 2025</a></div>
```

::: {.notes}
One report, three visual skills, three different pipelines. For charts, the authors synthesize about one million examples with matplotlib, seaborn and plotly: controlling chart type and values produces material for chart reading. Tables follow a different path: a recognition model processes six million real examples, then filtering removes low-confidence cases, overlapping tables and low cell density. Six million is the input count before filtering. For full document pages, the decisive choice is the target: an HTML representation that keeps recognized content, page structure, block positions and descriptions of illustrations. The target annotation defines which skill we ask the model to learn.

Next, video adds a time axis: first we must decide what counts as one training example.

**Sources:** [Qwen2.5-VL, §2.2.1, OCR Data](https://arxiv.org/html/2502.13923#S2.SS2.SSS1.Px4), [Document Omni-Parsing Data](https://arxiv.org/html/2502.13923#S2.SS2.SSS1.Px3).
:::

## A video file is not yet a training example {#data-video-boundaries .fv-slide .mv-slide background-color="#ffffff"}

```{=html}
<div class="fv-meta"><span class="fv-id">D 39 / 42</span><span class="fv-cluster">Architecture</span><span class="fv-cluster active">Data</span><span class="fv-cluster">Training</span><span class="fv-cluster">Inference</span><span class="fv-cluster">Tools</span></div>
<div class="fv-body dc-body d39-panda">
  <div class="dc-kicker"><b>Panda-70M · original Figure 2</b><span>From a long video to captioned clips</span></div>
  <figure><img src="assets/data_long_context_20261028/panda-figure2.png" alt="Original Panda-70M pipeline. A long video is split at shot boundaries and similar clips are stitched. Multiple teachers use video, frames and text to propose captions; a retrieval model selects the caption for each clip." /></figure>
  <div class="dc-pipeline"><div class="dc-step"><h3>1 · Find boundaries</h3><p>Split at shot changes.</p></div><div class="dc-arrow">→</div><div class="dc-step fragment" data-fragment-index="1"><h3>2 · Stitch clips</h3><p>Merge similar neighbors.</p></div><div class="dc-arrow fragment" data-fragment-index="1">→</div><div class="dc-step fragment" data-fragment-index="2"><h3>3 · Add a caption</h3><p>Generate candidates; select one.</p></div></div>
</div>
<div class="fv-takeaway fragment" data-fragment-index="2">Find boundaries. Repair unnecessary cuts.</div>
<div class="fv-source"><a href="https://arxiv.org/html/2402.19479v1#S3.SS1">Panda-70M, §3.1 and Appendix A; Figure 2</a> · Original Figure 2; three preparation steps summarized below</div>
```

::: {.notes}
A video file must be divided into useful examples. The original Panda-70M Figure 2 shows shot-boundary splitting followed by semantic stitching, then multiple captioning teachers and a retrieval model that selects an annotation. The figure is shown at full width to keep its internal labels readable.

**First click.** Emphasize stitching: Panda-70M uses ImageBind representations to merge similar neighboring pieces, with additional checks described in §3.1 and Appendix A. A shot change and a training-example boundary are not always the same thing; merging repairs excessive splitting rather than joining arbitrary neighbors.

**Second click.** Emphasize caption generation and selection for the resulting clip. The takeaway returns to choosing and repairing boundaries before treating a video as training data.

**Speaker-only reserve — retired teaching illustration, not on the current slide.** An 8-second cooking sequence had four pieces after cuts at 2, 4 and 6 seconds, then a merge of the two middle mixing segments with the 2- and 6-second boundaries retained. It illustrated the same preparation decisions, with no measured similarity scores or claim that the cuts were actual algorithm outputs.

Source: [Panda-70M, Figure 2, §3.1 and Appendix A](https://arxiv.org/html/2402.19479v1).
:::


::: {.notes}
Reveal sound and transcript, then word boundaries, then the video track. The vertical marker connects mouth shape, waveform and the active word. Deliberately shift the transcript at click four; restore it on click five. The words and recording have not become individually worse, but the mismatched pairing changes supervision.

Whisper supplies an audio/text task format with language and timing markers. LRS3-TED is an English audiovisual corpus, not evidence of multilingual coverage. ASR consumes audio and predicts words; TTS reverses the main direction, and audiovisual recognition can also use face video. Bridge to D 33: spoken image descriptions pass through ASR, so transcription quality matters for the final caption.

**Sixth click: language, locale, switching and recording quality.** The new scene replaces the alignment example. It separates language from local pronunciation and switching within an utterance. The bilingual phrase and two waveforms are schematic.

**Speaker-only source detail.** Sonic 3.6 lists 44 languages and 61 locales; Gemini 3.8 Flash TTS lists over 130 languages. These capability counts do not establish training proportions or source composition. ElevenLabs professional voice-cloning guidance recommends clean recordings and avoiding noise, reverberation and clipping; that concerns user samples, not proof about Eleven v4's training corpus. The selected pages do not disclose a full corpus.

Sources (checked 21 October 2026): [Whisper §2.1 / Figure 1](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2212.04356); [LRS3-TED](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1809.00496); [Sonic 3.6](https://www.cartesia.ai/blog/sonic-3.6); [Gemini TTS](https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/speech-generation); [Voice cloning recordings](https://elevenlabs.io/docs/eleven-creative/voices/voice-cloning/professional-voice-cloning).
:::

::: {.notes}
The cup pair is an original vector teaching example at identical scale. The requested change is only color; the background, table, shadow and geometry stay fixed. Reveal the optional mask and color reference separately from the core triplet. Then show the matrix of available input fields and finally highlight preserved content.

InstructPix2Pix's base task uses source, instruction and target without requiring a mask. MagicBrush contains manually annotated editing triplets and discusses both mask-provided and mask-free settings. Our three-row matrix is conceptual: it does not disclose proportions of any commercial model's training mixture, and a reference or mask is not universally present. Task mixtures vary which fields are inputs and which outputs must be predicted. Learning to preserve unmentioned content is part of successful editing.

Sources (checked 21 October 2026): [InstructPix2Pix Figure 2](https://arxiv.org/html/2211.09800v2); [MagicBrush](https://osu-nlp-group.github.io/MagicBrush/).
:::

## Data programs the model, in both directions {#data-still-open .fv-slide background-color="#ffffff"}

```{=html}
<div class="fv-meta"><span class="fv-id">D 42 / 42</span><span class="fv-cluster">Architecture</span><span class="fv-cluster active">Data</span><span class="fv-cluster">Training</span><span class="fv-cluster">Inference</span><span class="fv-cluster">Tools</span></div>
<div class="fv-body dc-body">
  <div class="dc-kicker"><b>Still open</b><span>Experiment · Anthropic, UK AISI, Alan Turing Institute, 2025</span></div>
  <div class="dc-two">
    <div class="dc-recipe"><h3>Open questions</h3><p>Synthetic text is already in the web.</p><p>Open training data is shrinking.</p><p>“Quality” depends on the target tasks.</p></div>
    <div class="dc-recipe fragment" data-fragment-index="1"><h3>Data poisoning</h3><div class="dc-metric"><b class="dc-number">≈250</b><span>documents</span></div><p>enough to plant a backdoor in models from 600M to 13B parameters.</p><p class="dc-caption">The absolute count matters, not the share of the corpus.</p></div>
  </div>
</div>
<div class="fv-takeaway fragment" data-fragment-index="1">Data programs the model — in both directions.</div>
<div class="fv-source"><a href="https://www.anthropic.com/research/small-samples-poison">Anthropic, UK AI Security Institute and Alan Turing Institute, A small number of samples can poison LLMs of any size, 2025</a></div>
<script src="assets/missed_slides_data_20261021/print-scenes.js"></script>
```

::: {.notes}
Three questions stay open: synthetic text already enters the web, open training data is shrinking, and "quality" depends on the target tasks.

**First click: data poisoning.** In 2023 Karpathy ended his LLM talk with data poisoning and said he knew no convincing demonstration for pre-training. In 2025 Anthropic, the UK AI Security Institute and the Alan Turing Institute showed that about 250 poisoned documents suffice to plant a backdoor in models from 600M to 13B parameters; the absolute count matters, not the share. Everything in this section used data to shape the model deliberately. The same lever works against us. Data programs the model, in both directions.

Next comes Training: which training signals these data provide and what each of them shapes in the model.

**Source:** [Anthropic, UK AISI and Alan Turing Institute, 2025](https://www.anthropic.com/research/small-samples-poison).

Watermarks mark the signal, while [C2PA](https://spec.c2pa.org/specifications/specifications/2.2/explainer/Explainer.html) signs provenance assertions and can use durable credentials and soft bindings; neither proves factual truth or human origin when absent. [SynthID](https://deepmind.google/models/synthid/) can alter text token-choice statistics; [Gemini replicated voices](https://blog.google/innovation-and-ai/models-and-research/gemini-models/gemini-3-8-text-to-speech/) combine SynthID and C2PA. [Qwen](https://www.alibabacloud.com/help/en/model-studio/qwen-audio-tts-http-api) documents an optional invisible AIGC identifier (enable_aigc_tag defaults to false), distinct from those mechanisms. [ElevenLabs](https://elevenlabs.io/docs/eleven-creative/audio-tools/audio-detector) checks its own watermark and may fall back to a speech classifier with limited third-party coverage: detected, not detected and insufficient evidence remain different outcomes (selected product sources checked 21 October 2026).
:::
